messages:
maya: heads-up — thinking about quarantining sampled traces that contain PII instead of sending them into the general telemetry pipeline. separate store, stricter RBAC, short TTL, audit-only inspection. want to surface tradeoffs before RFC.

liam: +1 to separation. two quick questions: 1) how do we decide "contains PII" reliably at ingest? 2) retention and access workflow? false positives could be expensive.

sasha: we propose a layered detection approach: deterministic detectors (emails, ssn regex), heuristic ML classifier for fuzzy cases, and a `scrub_status` enum that can be `clean | uncertain | pii_detected`. quarantine if `pii_detected` OR `scrub_status == uncertain && consent == "no"`. :thinking_face:

maya: sample routing config (proto):
```yaml
routing_rule: 
  id: quarantine-if-pii
  condition: "pii_detected == true or (scrub_status == 'uncertain' and consent == 'no')"
  action: send_to_quarantine
  quarantine_ttl_days: 30
  inspect_quota_per_month: 5
```

raj: quick API design question — should clients proactively send a consent header (eg `x-rw-consent: none|partial|full`) or should server-side detection be authoritative? pros/cons: headers make it explicit, but we can't trust all clients.

ellie: console UX note: any inspection should be a formal request flow in the console — require justification, auto-fill tenant+trace, one-click SRE approval for break-glass with ephemeral 20m tokens, and a recorded audit entry. also show remaining `inspect_quota` for tenant. :eyes: 

liam: quota model sounds right. suggest per-tenant monthly inspection credits; overflow requires manual ops review. also we should decrement quota on every successful inspect, and surface usage in the billing dashboard.

sasha: encryption: keep quarantined payloads encrypted with envelope keys. prefer per-tenant envelope key (KMS) to limit blast radius. fallback: service-level key for legacy tenants.

maya: canary plan: start with internal tenants + 0.5% of sampled traces from prod routed to quarantine, monitor false-positive rate and queue growth for 2 weeks. if <1% FP and storage growth acceptable, widen to 5%.

raj: debugging ergonomics — devs need some level of context without full PII. idea: return a tokenized anonymized snapshot (PII replaced with stable pseudonyms) for first-line triage. full plaintext requires inspect approval.

ellie: console mockups: modal will present anonymized snapshot + "request full inspect" button. request flow captures justification + approver list. show TTL and encrypted key metadata.

liam: operations — we need alerts when quarantine ingestion rate grows > 2x baseline for 12h, and a cost alarm for storage > threshold. also add a retention sweep job metric.

maya: edgecase: multi-tenant requests (shared prompts). we should tag traces with `tenant_scope: mixed` and default to quarantine unless explicit cross-tenant consent present.

sasha: scrubber false-positive mitigation: add `quarantine_reason` field so reviewers see why it was quarantined (regex, classifier, client-flag). makes audits easier.

devex-bot: deploy scheduled: canary branch `quarantine-routing` -> staging at 2026-03-22T10:00Z, PR #789 created by @maya. :rocket:

raj: one more: access controls — prefer RBAC groups (SRE, Security, SE with justification) plus time-limited tokens, and automatic audit entries shipped to audit-log index. no direct DB reads.

maya: OK next steps (agreed):
- maya: draft RFC w/ routing rules + KMS approach + canary plan
- ellie: console inspect flow mocks + approval UX
- sasha: run scrubber FP evaluation on last 7d sampled traces and share numbers
- liam: quota + billing signal spec, alert thresholds

ellie: assigning in-thread: @maya, @ellie, @sasha, @liam. will sync next Wed. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks everyone — will file RFC today and ping this thread when ready.
